newsitem.title: USA: FCC Hundt hopes to put off subsidy move a year - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: FCC Hundt hopes to put off subsidy move a year - WSJ.

text.p: Federal Communications Commission chairman Reed Hundt wants to postpone a key step in changing phone service subsidies until next year, the Wall Street Journal said in Tuesday's electronic edition.

The FCC should work with state regulators to calculate the costs of "universal service" in rural and high-cost areas while putting an interim system in place which would delay big changes in phone company competition until next year, Hundt was quoted in the newspaper as saying in an interview.
The FCC is trying to develop rules by next month to reduce access charges and overhaul the system that ensures low-income and rural Americans get quality and affordable phone service.
At the beginning of April, Hundt criticized a plan proposed by AT&T, Bell Atlantic and NYNEX which they said would cut customer phone bills $400 million a year.
